hero.description: Avernsys builds Rotasal: route optimization and fleet operations for last-mile delivery — the part of logistics that costs the most and is still run on spreadsheets.

story.title: Why we exist
paragraphs: Most last-mile fleets still plan the day by hand. Routes for dozens of vehicles are drafted in a spreadsheet, pushed to drivers over WhatsApp, and replanned by phone when the day goes sideways. Fuel and driver hours dominate the cost of every drop — and once a van leaves the depot, nobody can see it.

Rotasal replaces that with one system from dispatch desk to doorstep: dispatchers upload the day’s orders and get optimized, driver-ready routes from a native optimization core built in Rust; drivers get an app that keeps working in dead zones; every customer gets a live tracking link. Road graphs and traffic patterns are already modelled for twelve cities across Türkiye, Europe and the United States — Istanbul, our largest market, among them.
Avernsys Inc. was incorporated in Delaware in 2026; the team works from Palo Alto, California. One product, one operational problem — built by people who ship.

doruk.bio: Designed and shipped the whole Rotasal platform himself — the Rust optimization core, the dispatch backend, the courier and tracking apps, and the infrastructure they run on. Before Avernsys: engineer at Amazon and on Tesla’s autonomous-driving team, computer-vision research at UCLA, and the Starlink market-entry study for SpaceX in Türkiye. Computer engineering, Koç University.

items.title: Measured, not promised
items.description: Every claim can be checked on your own orders. Rotasal runs the optimizer against a human-dispatch baseline, cost line by cost line — and if the savings aren’t real, you’ll see that too.

items.title: Your data stays yours
items.description: Self-hosted maps and models, an on-premises option, and customer data that is never shared, sold, or used to train models. GDPR and KVKK by design.

items.title: Boring on purpose
items.description: Deterministic, reproducible solves; layered fallbacks so a failed solve degrades safely instead of hanging; a driver app that survives dead zones. A 5 a.m. dispatch desk has no room for surprises.
